candidates.tagline: Amazon's 'artificial AI' — humans pretending to be bots — shut down by actual AI
candidates.story: Amazon announced on August 26, 2026 that it's shutting down Mechanical Turk (MTurk) on September 30 — the platform Jeff Bezos called 'artificial artificial intelligence' because it used human workers to perform tasks too hard for real AI; after 21 years of humans training AI, the AI got good enough to replace them.
candidates.why_funny: The platform was literally named after an 18th-century chess automaton that hid a human grandmaster inside a fake robot — and now the fake AI has been defeated by the real thing it spent two decades helping build.
candidates.alt: A museum replica of the 18th-century Mechanical Turk chess automaton — a wooden cabinet with a mechanical arm and a mannequin in Ottoman dress, the famous hoax that concealed a human chess master inside the machine

candidates.tagline: Council's new cycle lane is narrower than the parking lines underneath it
candidates.story: Brighton and Hove Council repainted a cycle lane on Dyke Road in August 2026 during road resurfacing — producing a lane so narrow it barely extends beyond the double-yellow parking restriction lines already on the road, prompting cyclists to call it 'impressively dumb' and a 'box ticking exercise.'
candidates.why_funny: The council technically fulfilled its obligation to build cycling infrastructure, but delivered a lane so narrow cyclists say it's safer to ignore it and ride in traffic — meaning the only effect of the work is a fresh coat of paint that still helps nobody.
candidates.alt: A narrow cycle lane on Dyke Road, Brighton, so thin it barely extends beyond the double yellow no-parking lines painted beneath it — the white lane markings almost indistinguishable from the yellow parking restrictions they sit on top of
